newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian president nominates ally to head spy agency.
newsitem.headline: Romanian president nominates ally to head spy agency.

text.p: President Emil Constantinescu on Sunday nominated a close political ally to head Romania's intelligence service, whose former chief quit amid allegations of involvement in illegal activities.
A statement from Constantinescu's office proposed Costin Georgescu, 55, as director of the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) and described him as a "close colleague" of the president.

Georgescu was Constantinescu's chief fund-raiser in the presidential election that brought him to power last November and main political strategist in the 1992 campaign in which Constantinescu finished a distant second.
He was elected to parliament last year for the Democratic Convention, the electoral bloc forming the backbone of the centrist coalition backing the president.
The appointment has to be approved by both houses of parliament, where the coalition enjoys a large majority. He must give up his seat in the lower house of parliament.

Virgil Mugureanu was the first head of the SRI, which emerged as the successor to the all-pervasive communist-era Securitate in 1990, months after the bloody upheaval which toppled dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
Many Romanians believe the former Securitate still influences public life. Sunday's statement said Georgescu had assured the president "he had had no links whatsoever with the Securitate".
Magureanu left the job last month but had indicated his intention to resign before Constantinescu's election victory last November over ex-communist Ion Iliescu.

Mugureanu's spokesman had made plain that he was leaving his job after the new government had come under pressure from diplomats for him to go. In a parliamentary debate last month on SRI activity, liberal members accused him of meddling in politics to block reforms.

Mugureanu was one of several witnesses filmed attending the summary trial of Ceausescu and his wife Elena after they fled Bucharest during the December 1989 uprising against communist rule. Both were executed on Christmas Day.
